1.1 To ensure an established initial assessment.

2.0 SCOPE:

2.1 Hospital Management

2.2 Health Care Providers

2.3 Patients

2.4 Government agencies

3.0 RESPONSIBILITY:

3.1 Doctors, Hospital Management

3.2 Nursing staff

4.0 ABBREVIATIONS:

4.1 AAC - Access Assessment and Continuity of Care

5.0 DEFINITION: Nil

6.0 REFERENCE:

6.1 NABH: Accreditation Standards For Ayurveda Hospitals 2nd Edition April 2016.

7.0 OBJECTIVE ELEMENTS

7.1. The organisation defines and documents the content of the initial assessment for the outpatients, inpatients and emergency patients.

7.2 The organisation determines who can perform the initial assessment.

7.3. The organisation defines the time frame within which the initial assessment is completed based on patient needs.

7.4. The initial assessment for inpatients is documented within 24 hours or earlier as per the patient’s condition or hospital policy. Initial assessment includes identification of the medication that the in-patient is using of the relevant AYUSH system, of any other AYUSH system and of modern medicine.

7.5. Initial assessment includes screening for nutritional needs.

7.6 The care plan has to be documented and is monitored after the initial assessment.

7.7 The care plan also includes preventive aspects of the care where appropriate.

7.8 The care plan is countersigned by the doctor in-charge of the patient within 24 hours.

7.9. The care plan includes the desired results of the treatment, care or service.

8. 0 PROCESSES

8.1 INITIAL ASSESSMENT

8.1.2 Assessment of patients in the Outpatient department is done by the Consultant. History and Physical examination of the patient is written in the OPD form and prescription is given to the patient .

8.1.3 Initial Assessment for In-Patient to be carried out by,Treating Doctor or his / her Team Member within one hour of admission to determine immediate care needs and to decide on plan of care.

8.1.4 In case of emergency initial assessment will be completed immediately by treating doctors and the team as per patient's condition.

8.1.5 Nursing Initial Assessment is done within 30 minutes of patient admission into the ward.

8.1.6 The Treating Doctor and dietician should assess the nutritional needs of the Patient.

8.1.7 The Treating Doctor should document the plan of care and countersign based on initial assessment within 24 hours and is monitored after the initial assessment.

8.1.8 This plan of care should include preventive aspects of the care, e.g. Diet, Drugs, etc.

8.1.9 The care plan includes desired results of the treatment, care or service

8.1.10 The contents are Complaints, History, examination, Provisional Diagnosis/ Diagnosis, Investigations & treatment.

CONTENT OF THE INITIAL ASSESSMENT

INPATIENT & EMERGENCY PATIENTS

The Contents are Complaints, History, examination, Provisional Diagnosis / Diagnosis, Investigations & treatment.

OUTPATIENT AND DAY CARE

The patient form has the following parameters

a) Complaints with duration and history

b) Physical Findings

c) Clinical Diagnosis

d) Investigations

e) Treatment and follow-up
